title: Correct speed at B
description: Essential: The final numerical answer for the speed at point B must be 8 m/s.

title: Correct energy loss
description: Essential: The final numerical answer for the mechanical energy loss from A to C must be 5 J.

title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Important: The solution must apply the work-energy theorem correctly between points B and C, relating gravitational work to kinetic energy change.

title: Electric field work identification
description: Important: The solution must recognize that the electric field force does work from A to C, and this work is calculated via energy conservation.

title: Geometry for gravitational work
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the geometry (R and 30° angle) to find the vertical drop from B to C as R sin 30°.

title: Mechanical energy loss definition
description: Important: The solution must correctly state that the loss of mechanical energy equals the magnitude of the work done by the electric field force.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All quantities should be expressed with correct SI units (m, m/s, J, kg) throughout the calculation.

title: Sign error in electric work
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the sign of the electric field force's work is mistaken (it is negative, but the energy loss is positive).

title: Incorrect height for B-C
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the vertical distance from B to C is incorrectly taken as R, R cos 30°, or another wrong geometric expression.
